title: Baloot
tagline: The partnership card game of the Gulf
description: Baloot is the traditional four-player partnership card game of Saudi Arabia and the Gulf, related to the French game Belote. Bid for Sun (no trump) or Hokum (a trump suit where the Jack and 9 outrank the Ace), then play all eight tricks with your computer partner against two computer opponents. Ten hands-on lessons teach the whole game, four computer levels give you room to grow, and a new daily deal tests your reading of the table every day. Score only: no wagering, no ads, works offline. A full in-app Rules reference covers every ruling in detail.
howToPlay: New to Baloot? Tap Learn to play: ten short lessons where you make every real move yourself.
TAP a card to raise it, TAP it again to play it, or DRAG it upward. TAP a big button to bid.
Bidding: one card is turned face up. Say Hokum (that suit is trump), Sun (no trump, x2), or Pass.
Follow suit. In Hokum, if you can't and an opponent is winning, you must trump the trick.
In Hokum the Jack and 9 of trump outrank even the Ace.
Declare runs, sets or Baloot (King and Queen of trump) in the first trick for bonus points.
Hint (3 a hand) suggests a play and explains why. Take back undoes your last move.
Race to 152 (or a shorter 61) with your computer partner against two computer opponents.

title: Big Card Solitaire
tagline: Huge cards, tap to play, every deal winnable.
description: Big Card Solitaire is Klondike redrawn for comfort: oversized high-contrast cards, tap-to-move instead of dragging, and no timers or flashing effects. Every deal is checked so it can actually be won. A built-in "what can I do?" hint highlights your legal moves whenever you're unsure. An in-app Rules page explains every move in plain language.
howToPlay: Tap a card to select it, then tap where you want it to go - if only one move is legal, it plays automatically.
Build the four foundation piles up by suit, from Ace to King.
Stack tableau cards down in alternating colours.
Tap the stock pile to draw a new card when you're stuck.
Tap "what can I do?" any time to see every legal move highlighted.
Open Options any time to change the table colour, card back, 2- or 4-colour suits and motion. Your choices are remembered.

title: Carrom
tagline: Flick, pocket, cover the queen
description: Carrom is the flick-and-pocket board game played across South Asia, in homes, clubs and tournaments. Slide your striker along the baseline, pull back to aim and let go: coins slide, rebound off the cushions and drop into the corner pockets. Learn in eight hands-on lessons, play the computer at four levels or a friend on one phone, and try a new trick shot every day. A polished plywood board, glossy coins and a dotted aim guide that shows where each shot will go. Large text, reduced motion and left-handed layout included. An in-app Game Rules page covers every edge case. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: eight short lessons where you make every shot yourself.
DRAG the striker sideways along your baseline to place it. It turns red if it touches a coin.
DRAG BACK from the striker to aim. The dotted line shows the shot; a longer pull is a harder flick. RELEASE to flick.
Pocket a coin of your colour and you shoot again. Pocket nothing, or the other colour, and the turn passes.
Pocket the red queen, then pocket one of your own coins on the same or the next stroke to cover it, or she goes back.
Foul: if the striker falls into a pocket, one of your pocketed coins goes back to the centre and the turn passes.
Clear your coins first to win the board: 1 point for each coin left on the other side, plus 3 for the covered queen.
Keyboard: Left and Right slide, A and D aim, Up and Down set power, Space flicks. Hint shows a good shot.

title: Chess
tagline: The timeless game of sixty-four squares.
description: A complete, beautifully carved chess set: full rules including castling, en passant and promotion - with a full in-app rules reference for every piece and every way to win or draw - six AI levels from Beginner to Grandmaster, a 12-lesson tutorial, and a two-game AI vs AI demo to watch and learn from. Three original board themes with dimensional, carved-look pieces. Free to play, forever. No ads, no purchases.
howToPlay: TAP a piece to see its legal moves highlighted, then TAP a lit square to move it.
Or DRAG a piece to its destination and let go - both work everywhere.
Castle by TAPping or DRAGging the king two squares toward a rook.
Promote a pawn on the last rank by choosing Queen, Rook, Bishop or Knight in the picker.
Play White, Black, or pass-and-play Two Players on one device.
Choose an AI level from Beginner to Grandmaster, and use Undo or a Hint if you get stuck.
Learn the rules and basic tactics in 12 hands-on lessons.
Watch two full AI vs AI games play out end to end from the title screen.

title: Congklak
tagline: The shell game of Southeast Asia
description: Congklak (Congkak in Malaysia, Sungka in the Philippines) is the carved-boat mancala of Southeast Asia: seven houses a side, seven shells in each, both players sowing at once to open. Sow one shell at a time, scoop on when you land on a full house, shoot the house opposite when you land in an empty one, and play again when you end in your storehouse. Nine hands-on lessons, five computer levels, a daily puzzle and pass-and-play. Burnt houses raise the stakes each round. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: nine short lessons where you make every move yourself.
TAP a glowing house in your right-hand column to sow it. TAP anywhere while shells move to fast-forward.
Shells go one to each place ahead, into your storehouse but never your opponent's.
Last shell in your storehouse: play again. In a full house: scoop it up and keep sowing.
Last shell in your own empty house: shoot, taking every shell in the house opposite.
Each round starts with both players sowing at the same moment.
A round ends when the player to move has no shells; houses that cannot be refilled are burnt shut.
Undo takes back a move; Hint (3 per game) shows a good move and why.

title: Crown Fields
tagline: One crown per row, column and region. No touching.
description: Crown Fields is a calm grid-placement puzzle: place one crown in every row, column and coloured region so that no two crowns touch, even diagonally. Every puzzle is generated fresh with exactly one solution, solvable by pure logic. Play a quick 7x7, take on the tougher 10x10 Expert board, or try the Daily Puzzle. A free Hint and Undo are always there if you get stuck. An in-app Rules page explains every mechanic. No timers, no pressure - just clean logic.
howToPlay: Tap a cell to cycle it: empty, then crossed out, then a crown.
Placing a crown automatically crosses out every cell it would make illegal.
Every row, column and coloured region needs exactly one crown.
No two crowns may touch, even diagonally.
Fill the whole board correctly to solve the puzzle.
Stuck? Tap Hint for a free crown placement, or Undo to take back your last move.
Choose Play 7x7 or Expert 10x10 from the title screen, or try the Daily Puzzle.
Tap Colours on the title screen or while playing to change the region colours - your choice is remembered.

title: Durak
tagline: The card game of the fool
description: Durak, widely regarded as the most played card game of Russia and its neighbours: attack, defend, throw in, and try not to be the last one holding cards. Play against one to three computer players in Podkidnoy or Perevodnoy, learn in eight short lessons, solve a daily endgame and read the story of the game. A full in-app Rules reference covers every mechanic. Offline, score-only, no wagers.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: eight short lessons where you make every move yourself.
TAP a card to lift it, TAP it again to play it. Or DRAG it onto the table.
Beat an attack with a higher card of the same suit, or with a trump.
TAP Take to pick up the table when you cannot or will not beat.
Throw in cards whose rank is already on the table; TAP Bito when done.
Refill to six from the stock. The last player holding cards is the fool.
Hint (3 a match) shows a good move and why. Undo takes back your last move.
Daily Deal: both hands face up. Only one first move keeps you safe; find it, then play on.

title: Fox and Geese
tagline: One fox. A flock of geese. A cross of frost.
description: Fox and Geese is the classic hunt game, played on a cross of 33 points across Europe for centuries. One fox faces thirteen geese: the geese step forward or sideways and never back, and try to close the fox in; the fox slips between them and jumps any goose left alone, chaining jumps in one turn. Learn in nine hands-on lessons, play either side against four computer levels or a friend on one phone, choose a flock of 7 to 17 geese, and solve a new puzzle every day. Hand-painted fox and geese on a moonlit board. An in-app Rules page covers it all. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: nine short lessons where you make every move yourself.
The geese move first. Tap a goose (its points glow), then tap where it steps: one point forward or sideways, never backward.
The fox steps one point up, down, left or right, or jumps over a goose to the empty point behind it and captures it.
After a jump the fox may jump again in the same turn: tap a red point to go on, or tap the fox or Stop here to end its turn.
Move not allowed? The piece tries, comes back, and a message tells you why.
The geese win when the fox cannot move. The fox wins when only 5 geese are left. The same position three times is a draw.
Warnings mark geese the fox could take next. Hint shows a good move (3 per game). Take back undoes your last move.
Choose a flock of 7 to 17 geese (13 is classic). Beat each level with each side for a star. The daily puzzle is the same for everyone.

title: Go
tagline: The game of stones and territory
description: Go is the classic board game of East Asia: Weiqi in China, Baduk in Korea, Igo in Japan. Place stones on a kaya-wood board, surround territory and capture what has no liberties. Learn in eleven hands-on lessons, play the computer at four levels on 9x9, 13x13 or 19x19 boards, pass the phone to a friend, and solve a new puzzle every day. Dead stones are found for you, every refused move is explained, and hints say why a move is good. Hand-painted board, slate and shell stones, large text and reduced motion. An in-app Rules page covers every rule in exact detail. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: eleven short lessons where you make every move yourself.
TAP a crossing to aim: a ghost stone appears. TAP it again (or press Place) to play. DRAG to slide the ghost.
A stone or group with no empty neighbours (liberties) is captured. Playing where a stone would have none is not allowed.
Ko: you may not retake a single stone straight away. A move can never repeat an earlier whole-board position.
Pass when nothing useful is left. Two passes in a row end the game and the board is counted.
Scoring: your stones plus the empty points only you surround. White gets komi: 5.5 on 9x9, 7.5 on larger boards.
Dead stones are found for you: tap a group to change your mind, then Accept. Hint suggests a move and says why.
Four computer levels, three board sizes, two players on one phone, and a new daily puzzle with a streak.

title: Hare and Hounds
tagline: One hare. Three hounds. One narrow board.
description: Hare and Hounds is a traditional hunt game for two sides on a tiny board of eleven points. Three hounds close in on one hare, but hounds may never move backward, so every step is a promise. Trap the hare before the hunt clock runs out, or slip past the hounds. Learn in nine hands-on lessons, play either side at four computer levels, take on a twelve-level campaign with stars, solve a new puzzle every day, or play a friend on one phone. Hand-painted animals, large text and reduced motion. An in-app Rules page covers it all. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: nine short lessons where you make every move yourself.
One hare against three hounds. Tap a piece (its legal points glow), then tap where it goes. One step along a line per turn.
Hounds win by leaving the hare no move. They never capture, and may never move backward, only forward or sideways.
The hare wins by getting past all three hounds, or by lasting until the hunt clock (the hounds' moves) runs out.
Move not allowed? The piece tries, comes back, and a message tells you why.
Hare's reach shows where the hare could step next. Hint shows a good move (3 per game). Take back undoes your last move.
The campaign has twelve hunts: fewer moves earn more stars. The daily puzzle is the same for all, longer on weekends.
Beat each level with each side for a star. Winning unlocks new boards and a snowy set of pieces.

title: Golden Sling
tagline: Pull, aim, release. Guard the harvest.
description: A hand-carved slingshot, a golden field, and birds raiding the crop. Pull back, aim and release to scare them off before the harvest is gone. Every bird behaves differently, the wind picks up as you advance, and every miss sends the flock scattering. Free to play, with a new Daily Hunt every day. An in-app Rules page covers every bird and mechanic.
howToPlay: Drag back from the slingshot to aim - the dotted arc shows where the stone starts to fly.
Release to fire. Pull farther for more power; gravity and wind bend the shot.
Hit birds to scare them off and score. Hits in a row build a combo multiplier.
A miss costs the stone and startles nearby birds, so pick your shots.
Never hit the owl - it is protected and costs you stones.
Reach the level's quota before your stones or the crop runs out.

title: Tafl
tagline: The king's table of the North
description: Tafl is Hnefatafl, the Viking-age strategy game of Northern Europe. A king and his twelve defenders, surrounded by twenty-four attackers, must break out to any corner of the board before the ring closes or the king is taken. Play Copenhagen 11x11, the modern standard board, or start on the smaller, quicker Brandubh 7x7. Learn in ten hands-on lessons where you make every move yourself, play either side against four computer levels or a friend on one phone, and solve a new proven puzzle every day. Carved oak board, bone and horn pieces, hearth light, no ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: ten short lessons where you make every move yourself.
TAP a piece (its reachable squares glow), then TAP a square to move. Or DRAG and drop.
Every piece slides like a rook: any distance in a straight line, never jumping.
Trap an enemy piece between two of yours in a line to capture it. Moving in between two enemies is always safe.
The defenders' king reaches any corner to win. The attackers win by taking the king or ringing in every defender.
Move not allowed? The piece tries, comes back, and a message tells you why.
Warnings show the king's open lines to a corner. Hint gives a good move and why (3 per game). Take back undoes your last move.
Beat each level with each side, on both boards, for a star. The daily puzzle is the same for everyone; keep a streak.

title: Konane
tagline: The jumping game of Hawaii
description: Konane is a traditional Hawaiian strategy game: black and white stones fill a carved lava-stone slab, and every move is a jump that removes the stone you hop over. Whoever cannot jump loses. Learn with eight hands-on lessons, watch a full free Auto Play demonstration that thinks, reveals and plays every move for you, play a computer at four levels on 6x6, 8x8 or 10x10 boards, or solve a new daily puzzle where exactly one first jump wins by force. A full in-app Rules page covers the opening, the jump and how the game is won.
howToPlay: TAP one of your stones, then TAP a glowing square to jump there.
Jump over a touching enemy stone into the empty square behind it.
Keep hopping in one straight line, or stop after any hop.
You cannot turn a corner in one move, and you must jump if you can.
The first player with no jump left loses. There are no draws.
Eight lessons teach every rule by doing, or watch free Auto Play think and play a full game for you.
Take back moves and ask for hints that explain why.
Solve the daily puzzle: only one first jump wins.

title: Mahjong
tagline: The game of the four winds
description: Mahjong is the four-player tile game of China, played around the world. Build four sets and a pair before three computer players do: draw, discard, and call chows, pungs and kongs. Hong Kong-style scoring shows exactly which patterns scored and why. Learn in eleven hands-on lessons, watch free Auto Play play a whole hand face-up for you, play three computer levels, get plain-words hints, and solve a new discard puzzle every day. Thick ivory-and-jade tiles, a felt table, large text, reduced motion and three tile-face styles. Play in 中文 or English. Score only, no ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Eleven short lessons teach every step, or watch free Auto Play play a whole hand face-up for you.
Each turn you draw a tile and discard one. TAP a tile to lift it, then TAP it again (or DRAG it up) to discard.
Build four sets and a pair: a chow is three in a row in one suit, a pung is three alike, a kong is four alike.
When another player discards a tile you can use, TAP Chow, Pung, Kong or Win!, or TAP Pass. A short timer runs; you can turn it off.
Win! beats Pung and Kong, which beat Chow. A chow may only be taken from the player before you.
A win needs at least 1 fan (or 3 in Settings). The score screen shows each pattern and why it scored.
Tap Why? for advice on your discard. The daily challenge is three puzzles, the same for everyone.
Play a Quick hand or a whole East round of four deals. Your hand is saved when you leave.

title: Nine Men's Morris
tagline: The mill game of Europe
description: Nine Men's Morris, known as Muhle in Germany, Moulin in France and Merels in England, is a medieval mill game carved into cloister seats across Europe. Place nine men on a 24-point board, slide them along the lines and take an enemy man with every row of three. Learn in ten hands-on lessons, watch a free Auto Play demonstration play a whole game for you, play five computer levels from Apprentice to Grandmaster, pass the phone to a friend, and solve a mill puzzle every day. Every rule is written out in full on the in-app Rules page. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Ten short lessons teach every move, or watch free Auto Play play a whole game for you.
Placing: Light starts. Tap an empty point to place a man. Each side places nine.
Sliding: tap a man, then a glowing point beside it (or drag it there). Men slide one step along a line.
Three men in a row is a mill. Tap a glowing red enemy man to take it. Men in a mill are safe unless all enemy men are in mills.
Down to three men? You fly: any man may jump to any empty point.
You win when the enemy has two men left or cannot move. Same position 3 times, or 50 moves each with no mill, is a draw.
A refused move shows a red ring and says why. Hint (3 per game) explains a good move. Undo takes back.
Five levels, a daily mill puzzle, boards and men to earn. Large text and calm (reduced motion) options.

title: Morabaraba
tagline: The game of twelve cows
description: Morabaraba is a traditional board game of Southern Africa, played in Lesotho, South Africa, Botswana and Zimbabwe. Twelve cows each on a board of three squares joined by lines and diagonals: place your herd, form a mill of three to shoot an opposing cow, slide to open and close mills, and fly when you are down to three. Learn in nine hands-on lessons, watch a free Auto Play demonstration play a whole game for you, play four computer levels or a friend on one phone, and solve a daily puzzle. Painted dusk-over-the-veld art, large text and reduced motion. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: nine short lessons where you make every move yourself.
Placing: TAP an empty point to place a cow. Each side places all twelve cows first.
Three cows in a line make a mill, diagonals included. Close one and TAP a glowing cow to shoot it.
A cow standing in a mill is protected, unless all of that side's cows are in mills.
Sliding: TAP a cow, then a glowing point (or DRAG it). Cows move one step along a line.
Down to three cows you may FLY a cow to any empty point. Fewer than three, or no move, loses.
Illegal move? The cow tries, comes back, and a message says why. Hints explain themselves.
Beat each computer level with each colour for a star. The daily puzzle is the same for all.
Auto Play (free, silent): watch a full game play itself - it pauses for you to think, then reveals and plays the move it chose.

title: Mū Tōrere
tagline: The eight-pointed star game of Aotearoa
description: Mū Tōrere is a traditional Māori board game of Aotearoa New Zealand. Four stones each sit on an eight-pointed star around a central pit, the putahi: slide one stone at a time and leave your opponent with no move. The game is tiny and fully solved, all traps and foresight. Learn in eight hands-on lessons, watch free Auto Play play a whole game for you, climb a Ladder of twelve opponents, solve a new proven puzzle daily, or play a friend on one phone. Carved-wood board, shell and greenstone stones, calm sound. An in-app Rules page spells out every move. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Eight short lessons teach every move, or watch free Auto Play play a whole game for you.
TAP one of your stones (its legal points glow), then TAP a point. Or DRAG the stone there.
A stone moves one step: to the next point around the star, or between the rim and the putahi (centre).
A stone may enter the putahi only when it stands beside an enemy stone. From the putahi it may step to any empty point.
You win when your opponent has no legal move. The same position three times is a draw.
Move not allowed? The stone tries, comes back, and a message tells you why.
Hint shows a good move and why (3 per game). Take back undoes your move and the reply.
Climb the Ladder of 12 opponents. The last two cannot be beaten, only held to a draw.

title: One Arrow Oath
tagline: Nothing fires twice.
description: A deckbuilder where your best cards can be played only once. You are an archer sworn never to loose the same arrow twice: every named Arrow you play is spent for the whole run, so each fight asks how little you can afford to spend. Read every enemy's intent, answer it with the right element, take on Debts that come due at the worst moment, and decide whether to keep the Covenant or break it. Inspired by a warrior's vow from ancient Sanskrit epic poetry, one of the world's oldest literary traditions. The world and every name in it are original. An in-app Rules page covers every system.
howToPlay: Read the intent above each enemy: what it will do this turn, and which element answers it.
Press a card and pull it down like a bowstring, then release to play it. Tapping it twice also works.
Gold-framed Arrows hit hard and are spent for the whole run. Steel-framed Techniques come back.
Answer an attack with the element that beats it. A Ward cancels it; a matching Arrow also strikes for +50%.
Finish weak enemies with Reed Shafts. Never loose a named Arrow at a Lure - it will be wasted.
After each fight, take one new card. Camps heal, the Tuner trades, Envoys offer choices.
Debts give power now and come due in the final fight. Settle them at a Camp if you can.
Breaking the Covenant wins the moment, but Standing lost that way is hard to earn back.
New to it all? Tap Auto Play on the title screen to watch a whole run play itself, at a thinking pace you choose.

title: Oware
tagline: The seed-sowing game of West Africa
description: Oware is the classic seed-sowing game of Ghana and West Africa, part of the mancala family. Twelve pits, forty-eight seeds: lift a pit, sow seeds round the board, and capture pits that end with two or three. Learn in eight short hands-on lessons, watch free Auto Play play a whole game at your own pace, play the computer at five levels from Easy to Grandmaster, pass the phone to a friend, and solve a new capture puzzle every day. Hand-carved wood and glossy seed art, large text and reduced motion. Full rules are in the in-app Rules page. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Eight short lessons teach every move, or watch free Auto Play play a whole game at your own pace.
TAP one of your pits on the bottom row to sow it. Glowing pits are the ones you can play.
Seeds go one per pit, counter-clockwise: along your row, then back along your opponent's row.
If your last seed makes an opponent pit hold 2 or 3, you capture it, and the pits before it if they also hold 2 or 3.
A pit with 12 or more seeds laps the board and skips its own pit.
If your opponent has no seeds you must play a move that gives them some.
First to capture 25 seeds wins. Undo takes back a move; Hint (3 per game) shows a good move and why.
Daily puzzle: TAP the one pit that captures the most seeds. Same puzzle for everyone.

title: Pachisi
tagline: The royal race of the cross
description: Pachisi is the royal race game of India, ancestor of Ludo. Throw six cowrie shells, count the mouths that face up, and race four pawns around the embroidered cloth cross to its centre. Land on a rival to send it home, hide on the marked squares, block the way with a pair. Play the full game or the friendly Ludo mode, with two to four players, against four computer personalities or friends passing one phone. Nine hands-on lessons, Auto Play (a full game plays itself at a pace you set), a daily race and an exhaustive in-app Rules reference. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Nine short lessons teach every move, or watch free Auto Play play a whole game at your own pace.
TAP the cowries, or SWIPE up across them, to throw. Count the mouths facing up: 1 up = 10, 2 = 2, 3 = 3, 4 = 4, 5 = 25, 6 = 6, none = 12.
Grace throws (10, 25, 6, 12) give another throw and are the only throws that let a waiting pawn enter the board.
Pawns that can move glow. TAP one to see where it lands, then TAP it again to move it. A pawn that cannot move shakes and tells you why.
Race anticlockwise once around the cross, then up the middle lane to the centre. The centre needs an exact count.
Land exactly on a rival pawn to send it home. Squares marked with an X are safe; two of your pawns on one square form a block.
Play 2, 3 or 4 players against computers (Beginner, Cautious, Balanced, Bold) or pass one phone between friends.
Ludo mode uses one die and a smaller board. The daily race sets the same six throws for everybody.

title: Perch
tagline: Read the stone. Choose your moment.
description: You are a small bird on a branch, and hunters with catapults ring the field. You never aim: you read the stone coming and choose your moment to fly. Survive each day until sunset for up to three stars. Level 1 is one tree; from level 2 whole groves and orchards open up and you choose where to fly. Every level adds one new idea: golden seeds, fast archers, wind, a Master Hunter with a pattern to learn, nets and beaters. From level 3, close calls earn acorns to knock hunters flat. A hit only ruffles feathers. No ads, works offline. An in-game Rules page covers every mechanic in detail.
howToPlay: A hunter pulls back a catapult and a red ring shows the perch the stone will hit. A dotted arc shows its path.
Level 1: tap anywhere to fly and the bird picks the safest perch. From level 2, tap the perch you want to fly to.
Leave at the last moment for a close call (+5). Dodges in a row build a combo up to x5.
You have 3 feathers. Survive until the bar at the top fills (sunset): 3 stars for no hits.
Golden seeds: tap the perch that holds one to fly for it. Every third seed heals a feather.
Archers fire fast arrows. In wind, trust the red ring, not the hunter. Nets cover a whole tree: leave it. Beaters rattle your perch.
Hit back (level 3+): close calls earn acorns, up to 3. Tap a hunter to knock him down and cancel his shot.
Boss levels: the Master Hunter fires the same pattern every attempt. Learn it.

title: The Royal Game of Ur
tagline: A race from the cradle of civilisation
description: The Royal Game of Ur is the Game of Twenty Squares, played in Mesopotamia over four thousand years ago. Roll four pyramid dice and race seven inlaid pieces down your lane, up the shared middle lane and home. Rosettes are safe and give another roll; landing on an enemy sends it back. Learn in nine hands-on lessons, watch Auto Play demonstrate a whole game move by move at your own pace, play four computer levels or a friend, and solve a daily best-move puzzle. Lapis, shell and red-limestone art lit by an oil lamp. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Nine short lessons teach every move, or watch free Auto Play play a whole game at your own pace.
Tap the dice to roll four pyramid dice: each gold tip up counts 1, so a roll is 0 to 4.
Tap a glowing piece, then the glowing square it goes to. Moves are exact.
Your path: 4 squares in your lane, 8 in the shared middle lane, then 2 home. Rosettes give another roll.
Landing on an enemy piece in the middle lane sends it back. A piece on a rosette is safe.
The central rosette blocks the lane: nobody can land there while it is occupied.
A piece leaves the board only with the exact roll. First to bring all seven home wins.
Refused move? The piece tries and returns, and a message says why. Hints and Take back help.

title: Scopa
tagline: The Italian card game of the broom
description: Scopa is one of Italy's three major national card games, played with a 40-card Italian deck: coins, cups, swords and batons. Match a card's rank or a sum to capture it, clear the table for a scopa, and score cards, coins, sette bello and primiera. Nine hands-on lessons, free Auto Play at your own pace, four computer levels to a card-counting Maestro, four-player partnerships, and a new daily deal every day. Original hand-drawn Italian court cards, a trattoria table, and a French-suit option. No ads, no chips, score only.
howToPlay: New here? Nine short lessons teach every move, or watch free Auto Play play a whole game at your own pace.
TAP a card in your hand, then TAP a table card of the same rank to capture it.
If several table cards add up to your card's rank, TAP each one to take the whole set.
A matching card must always be taken alone, even when a sum is also possible.
Clear the table and you score a scopa: one point, shown with a flourish (not on the round's last play).
Nothing to capture? TAP your card again to lay it on the table.
A round is scored on most cards, most coins, the sette bello and primiera. Play to 11 or 21.
Daily deal: find the single most valuable capture. Same deal for everyone, every day.

title: Senet
tagline: The board game of ancient Egypt
description: Senet is the board game of ancient Egypt, played for thousands of years and shown in tomb paintings. Throw four sticks, race five pieces along a 30-square path, swap lone enemy pieces, hold a wall of three, and avoid the House of Water. Rules follow a widely published modern reconstruction. Learn in ten hands-on lessons, watch free Auto Play play a whole game at your own pace, play five computer levels or a friend, and solve a daily puzzle. Ebony-and-ivory board, gilded inlay, faience pieces, tumbling sticks. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Ten short lessons teach every move, or watch free Auto Play play a whole game at your own pace.
TAP the sticks to throw. Count the light faces: 1 to 4, or 5 if none. A 1, 4 or 5 earns another throw.
TAP a glowing piece, then TAP a glowing square. It moves exactly the number thrown, along the S-shaped path.
Land on a lone enemy piece to swap places. Pairs, and pieces on safe houses, cannot be swapped.
Three pieces in a row make a wall that nothing can pass. Every piece must stop on square 26.
Square 27 is the House of Water: it sends a piece back to 15. Leave with exact throws: 5 from 26, 3, 2 or 1 from 28-30.
A refused move shakes and tells you why. Hint shows a good move; Take back undoes yours.
First to bring all five pieces home wins. Beat each level for a star; a new puzzle every day.

title: Shogi
tagline: Japan's game of generals and drops
description: Shogi is the chess-like strategy game of Japan, played on a 9 by 9 board. Its big idea: a captured piece changes sides and can be dropped back on any empty point. Learn in twelve hands-on lessons where you make every move, play five computer levels from Novice to Master as either side, try the quick 5x5 mini board, or pass the phone to a friend. Every refused move is explained, hints tell you why, and a new checkmate puzzle arrives every day. Hand-drawn kaya board and boxwood pieces, large text and reduced motion options. No ads, works offline. Play in 日本語 or English. Full rules built in.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: twelve short lessons where you make every move yourself.
TAP one of your pieces: every point it may move to glows. TAP a glowing point to move.
Landing on an enemy piece captures it. Captured pieces wait on your stand under the board.
To drop: TAP a piece on your stand, then TAP an empty glowing point.
Reach the last three rows and you may promote: TAP Promote or Keep.
Not allowed? The piece tries and returns, and a message says why (check, nifu, blocked...).
Win by checkmate. Hint (3 per game) and Take back help you learn.
The puzzle of the day is mate in 1 on weekdays and mate in 3 at the weekend.

title: Sure Sweep
tagline: No-guess minesweeper. Every board solves by logic alone.
description: Sure Sweep is classic mine-clearing with one guarantee: every board can be fully solved by logic, with no lucky guesses required. Tap to reveal, flip the switch to flag suspected mines, and chord through satisfied numbers to clear the board fast. Stuck? A free hint shows you the deduction you missed, and one free Undo takes back a fatal tap. Sea-chart art, a calm teal palette, and colour schemes you can switch anytime. A full in-app Rules page covers every mechanic.
howToPlay: Tap a cell to reveal it.
A number shows how many mines touch that cell.
Flip the Reveal/Flag switch to Flag, then tap a cell to mark it as a suspected mine.
Tap a revealed number when its flags match it to clear the safe cells around it.
Reveal every non-mine cell to win - the board is guaranteed solvable without guessing.
Stuck? Tap Hint for a free forced move while you play.
Lose a board? Tap Undo once to take back the fatal tap and keep going.
Tap the colour button on the title screen or while playing to switch colour schemes - your choice is remembered.

title: Tarneeb
tagline: The partnership card game of the Levant
description: Tarneeb is the bidding-and-trump trick-taking card game of the Levant. You and a computer partner bid against two computer opponents for how many of 13 tricks your side will take; the winning bidder names trump and leads. Follow suit, take tricks, and score by what you win. Learn in eight hands-on lessons, play four computer levels with hints that explain the reasoning, and solve a new open-hand Daily Deal every day. An in-app Rules page covers bidding and scoring in full. Designed cards with a large-print option, a warm cafe table. No ads, offline, score only.
howToPlay: Four players, two partnerships: you and your partner against two computer opponents.
Bidding: each player bids 7 to 13 tricks or passes. High bidder names trump and leads.
TAP a card to lift it, TAP again (or DRAG it up) to play. You must follow the suit led.
Highest trump wins a trick; with no trump played, highest card of the suit led wins.
Make your bid and your side scores its tricks; fall short and your side loses the bid.
Eight lessons teach following suit, trump, bidding, partnership play and a full hand.
Daily Deal: all hands face up. Only one first card can reach the target; find it, then play it out.
Hint explains a good bid or card with a reason; Undo takes back your last move.

title: Tavla
tagline: The dice game of the coffeehouse
description: Tavla is backgammon as played in the coffeehouses of Turkey, the Arab world, Israel and Persia, also called tawla, shesh besh and takhteh nard. Race fifteen checkers around 24 points, hit lone checkers, build walls and bear off first. Learn in nine hands-on lessons, play four computer levels or a friend on one phone, and solve a new best-move puzzle every day. Hints explain why, undo is one tap, forced moves can play themselves. Optional score-only doubling cube and gammons. Inlaid wooden board, carved checkers, tumbling dice. Large text and reduced motion. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: TAP the dice to roll them: they tumble and settle.
TAP one of your checkers: the points it can reach glow. TAP a glowing point to move, or DRAG and drop.
Each die is one move; doubles are played four times. You must play as many dice as you can.
You cannot land on a point held by two or more opposing checkers. A lone checker (blot) that is hit goes to the bar.
A checker on the bar must enter first. A refused move explains why in plain words.
When all 15 are in your home board, bear them off. First to bear off all 15 wins; gammons score more.
TAP Undo to take back a move, Hint for a good play and its reason. Single forced moves can play themselves.
New here? Learn to play has nine short lessons. The daily puzzle is the same for everyone.

title: Tiger and Goat
tagline: Four tigers. Twenty goats. One board.
description: Tiger and Goat is Bagh-chal, Nepal's traditional board game. Four tigers hunt twenty goats on a board of 25 points: the goats are slow but many, the tigers few but fast. The game ends only when every goat is captured or every tiger is trapped. Learn in nine hands-on lessons, play either side against four computer levels or a friend on one phone, and solve a new puzzle every day. Win games to earn new boards and a snowy set of pieces. Hand-painted art, large text and reduced motion options. An in-app Rules page covers it all. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: nine short lessons where you make every move yourself.
Goats go first: tap an empty point to place one. All 20 must be placed before any goat may move.
To move, tap a piece (its legal points glow), then tap where it goes. Goats step one point along a line and never jump.
A tiger steps one point or jumps a goat to the empty point behind it, capturing it. Goats on an edge or with a piece behind are safe.
Move not allowed? The piece tries, comes back, and a message tells you why.
Tigers win by capturing every goat; goats win when no tiger can move. Five captures do not end it. Three repeats is a draw.
Warnings mark goats a tiger could take next. Hint shows a good move (3 per game). Take back undoes your last move.
Beat each level with each side for a star. The daily puzzle is the same for all, longer on weekends. Winning unlocks boards and pieces.

title: Toguz Kumalak
tagline: The nine-pebble game of the steppe
description: Toguz Kumalak is the traditional sowing game of Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, part of the mancala family. Eighteen pits, 162 pebbles: lift a pit, sow round the board, capture pits your last pebble makes even, and win one opponent pit for good as your tuz. Learn in ten short hands-on lessons, play the computer at five levels, pass the phone to a friend, and solve a new puzzle every day. An in-app Rules page covers every rule in full. Carved wood, felt and kilim-pattern art, large text and reduced-motion options. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: ten short lessons where you make every move yourself.
TAP one of your pits on the bottom row. Glowing pits are the ones you can play.
The first pebble stays in the pit; the rest go one per pit, counter-clockwise.
If your last pebble lands in an opponent pit and makes it even, you capture it.
If it makes exactly three, that pit becomes your tuz: every pebble landing there is yours.
One tuz each; never the opponent's 9th pit, never the same number as their tuz.
First to collect 82 of the 162 pebbles wins. Undo takes back a move; Hint shows why.
Daily puzzle: TAP the one pit that takes the most pebbles.

title: Word Game
tagline: Tap the matching word before it drifts away.
description: Word Game is a fast vocabulary drill built around over 300 graduate-level words. A target word appears at the top and three candidate words drift across the screen - tap the correct synonym or antonym before it drifts away. After every session you get a full review of each word: what you tapped, the correct answer and its meaning, so mistakes turn into words you remember. A full in-app Rules page explains every mechanic.
howToPlay: Choose Synonym or Antonym mode, then tap Play to start a 90-second session.
A target word appears at the top; three candidate words drift in from the right.
Tap the one word that correctly matches the target before it drifts off-screen.
A correct tap scores a point and the next word appears immediately.
A wrong tap, or letting the right word drift past, ends that word with no point - the next word appears right away.
Tap Stop any time to end the session early, or tap Watch & Learn for a free, untimed Auto Play demo that plays itself.
When the session ends, review every word: your answer, the correct answer and its meaning. Then play again to beat your best score.
Tap Colours on the title screen or while playing to switch colour schemes - the default is kept and your choice is remembered.

title: Xiangqi
tagline: The game of the river and the palace
description: Xiangqi is Chinese chess: two armies of sixteen carved pieces face each other across the river, each general guarded inside its palace. Cannons jump to capture, horses can be hobbled, and the generals may never face each other. Learn in ten hands-on lessons, play Red or Black against five computer levels or a friend on one phone, and solve a new checkmate puzzle every day. Play in 中文 with the traditional characters, or in English with Western piece letters. Two board styles, two piece sets, large text and reduced motion. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Ten short lessons teach every move, or tap Auto Play to watch a free demo play itself.
TAP one of your pieces: it lifts and its legal points glow. Then TAP a glowing point, or DRAG the piece there.
A red glow marks a piece you can capture. Cannons capture by jumping over exactly one piece.
Move not allowed? The piece tries, comes back, and a message tells you why.
Attack the enemy general so it cannot escape: that is checkmate. If you are in check you must answer at once.
Generals never face each other on an open file. A side with no legal move loses.
Hint shows a good move (3 per game). Undo takes back your move and the reply.
The daily puzzle is the same for everyone: mate in 2 on weekdays, mate in 3 at weekends.

title: Yut Nori
tagline: Korea's four-stick race
description: Throw four carved sticks and race your horse tokens round a paper board on a woven mat. Yut Nori is the traditional Korean game: yut and mo earn extra throws, corner shortcuts cut across the board, tokens stack to travel as one, and landing on a rival sends it back to the start. Learn in ten hands-on lessons, play a cautious, balanced or aggressive computer team, pass the phone between two teams, and try a new daily challenge. Hand-drawn art, sound, large text and reduced motion. No ads, works offline.
howToPlay: New here? Tap Learn to play: ten short lessons where you make every move yourself.
TAP the felt pad, or SWIPE up on it, to throw the four sticks. Flat sides up: 1 do, 2 gae, 3 geol, 4 yut, none mo (5).
Yut, mo and every capture earn another throw. Throws are kept and spent in any order: TAP a throw chip to choose one.
TAP a token, then TAP a glowing point to move. A token starting on a corner may take the diagonal shortcut.
Land on your own token to stack them; land on a rival to capture it and send it back to the start.
Back-do (the marked stick alone) moves a token one step back. Refused taps always tell you why.
Bring all four tokens home first to win. Hints, take back, five computer levels and a daily challenge help you learn.
Keyboard: Space throws, arrows pick token and point, Tab chooses a throw, H hint, U take back.
